# DESIGN.md

<!-- Generated by `npm run system` from design/system.yaml: change the record, not this file. -->

**Starter.** A warm off-white page that opens on the business's best photograph at full width, with one accent for every action, large and few headings, and a different shape for each section.

The tokens are compiled into `styles/theme.css`; `npm run check:design` reads the Declared section.

## Identity

```text
Subject:            to fill: what this site sells, explains, or does
Audience:           to fill: who arrives, and what they already know
One job:            to fill: what the page must make clear or help someone do
Direction:          to fill: the chosen direction's name and one-sentence thesis
Source:             to fill: the real-world artifact or behaviour it borrows from
Signature:          to fill: the one moment a visitor should remember
Rejection:          to fill: the familiar pattern this site deliberately avoids
Photography:        to fill: real photos the owner has, or the honest slot until they do
```

## Visual Theme & Atmosphere

A warm, quiet page where one thing is loud at a time. It opens on the business's best photograph edge to edge behind the headline. The ground is a warm off-white, the text a near-black with brown in it, and one saturated accent does every action. Headings are large and few, so hierarchy comes from size and space; colour and energy come from the business's own photographs and material. `npm run check:design` flags the generated-page patterns and the contrast.

## Color Palette & Roles

| Token | Value |
|---|---|
| `canvas` | #f6f3ec |
| `surface` | #fffdf8 |
| `panel` | #ebe5d8 |
| `night` | #14110d |
| `ink` | #191612 |
| `ink-2` | #57514a |
| `ink-3` | #6b5f54 |
| `night-ink` | #f6f3ec |
| `night-ink-2` | #bfb6aa |
| `accent` | #2f5bea |
| `accent-ink` | #ffffff |
| `accent-hover` | color-mix(in oklab, `accent` 85%, black) |
| `line` | rgb(25 22 18 / 0.14) |
| `line-strong` | rgb(25 22 18 / 0.32) |
| `line-on-night` | rgb(246 243 236 / 0.16) |

`canvas` is the page ground, `surface` a card or framed visual on it, `panel` a tinted band, `night` the dark ground (the first screen without a photograph, a statement band, the footer). `ink` is text on light grounds, `ink-2` secondary text, `ink-3` captions; on night, `night-ink` and `night-ink-2`. `accent` is the one action colour (buttons, links in copy, the focus ring), with `accent-ink` on it and `accent-hover` its hover. `line` is a hairline, `line-strong` an input edge, `line-on-night` a hairline on night.

## Typography Rules

| Class | Family | Size | Line height | Tracking | Weight |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `text-display` | Bricolage Grotesque | clamp(3rem, 8vw, 6rem) | 0.95 | -0.03em | 700 |
| `text-section` | Bricolage Grotesque | clamp(2.25rem, 5vw, 3.75rem) | 1 | -0.025em | 600 |
| `text-title` | Bricolage Grotesque | clamp(1.5rem, 2.4vw, 2rem) | 1.1 | -0.015em | 600 |
| `text-lede` | Inter | clamp(1.125rem, 1.4vw, 1.375rem) | 1.5 |  | 400 |
| `text-copy` | Inter | 1.125rem | 1.6 |  | 400 |
| `text-label` | Inter | 0.875rem | 1.4 | 0.04em | 600 |

A display face for headings, a text face for reading. `text-display` is the page's h1, on two or three lines; `text-section` every h2; `text-title` the h3 of a row or a card; `text-lede` the line under a heading, in `ink-2`; `text-copy` body text, under 70 characters a line; `text-label` metadata such as a date or a caption. Each size carries its own line height and tracking.

## Component Stylings

The first screen is Hero: the photograph, or a short muted video, full-bleed behind the headline, one line, one action and the RatingLine; with no photograph good enough, the words on `night`. One primary Button per section, labelled with what happens next. Cards hold discrete, comparable things (a service, a person, a review); a list reads better as rows. Images sit at `rounded-card`. The rest are in src/components (npm run parts).

## Layout Principles

Every band shares one frame, max-w-wide with px-5 sm:px-8 (Section does this), so the header, sections and footer start on one left edge; reading text narrows to max-w-content. Sections take py-section, and a heading sits mt-lead above what it introduces. Photographs run edge to edge where they are the point: the first screen's always, when the business has one, chosen by looking at them (brand/images.md). Add a section whenever the material has something a visitor would look for: a gallery, the team, the process, the area served. Compose each from its content, so a sequence, a comparison and a story look different and no two neighbours share a shape. One section is the peak; the rest are quieter.

## Depth & Elevation

Mostly flat. A card or framed visual that should feel like an object gets a `line` edge and `shadow-lift`; a menu or dialog sits on `surface` with `shadow-lift`; the team's admin cards get `shadow-card`.

## Motion

The first screen's words rise in once (data-rise), and one or two later bands as they come into view (data-reveal); a long row of reviews or logos may run as a marquee (data-marquee). Hover and focus take 150ms with `ease-soft`. Reduced motion shows the finished page (styles/input.css).

## Responsive Behavior

Phone and desktop are two compositions of the same content. Type is fluid, so headings need no phone sizes. Below 1024px a split stacks, text first unless the visual is the point; cards go to one column below 640px. The header stays one row; past four links the rest go into a menu.

## Do's and Don'ts

Do:

- Spend boldness in one place per page.
  When every section is loud, none is; the peak is what a visitor remembers.
- Use the tokens; add one to this record when one is missing.
  A one-off value in markup is a second design system that nobody maintains.

Don't:

- Don't default to a centred hero over a glow, three feature cards, pricing, an FAQ and a final call to action whatever the content.
  It is the generated-page template; a visitor has seen it a hundred times and it says nothing about this business.
- Don't use gradients, blur, glass or glow to make up for a weak idea.
  Effects date fast and hide that the section has nothing to show.
- Don't put a form beside the first headline, or a small label above the headline or above every heading.
  Both are the generated-page look; the first screen's job is the photograph and the promise.
- Don't reach for cream with a soft serif, or Inter with Playfair, by default.
  They are what generated sites pick; the type and colour come from the business or a library record.
- Don't leave a section that would fit another business with the logo swapped.
  It tells the visitor nothing about this one; their own facts, photographs and proof do.

## Known Gaps

No layout rules per kind of content: those come with the site's own system when it grows past the homepage.

## Changing the design

Edit `design/system.yaml` and run `npm run system`; then `npm run check:design`.
A new brand colour or font goes into the record's tokens by role, never into markup. How a record is
written, and how it grows from the first homepage, is the `design` skill.
